spacing.note: No mathematical grid — optical/poster composition with negative overlaps (-11px x20). 5px and 10px dominate at component level; 28/42/56px at block level.

colors.value: teal/cyan photographic gradient field (image, not CSS)

shadows: rgba(0,0,0,.19) 0 10px 20px, rgba(0,0,0,.23) 0 6px 6px (BOOK NOW only — sole offset shadow on page)

taste.name: The Poster Is the Website
taste.trigger: When the show's chromatic-aberration title treatment had to survive the trip from print campaign to browser
taste.decision: Shipped all headline typography as image assets (2000x955 webp lockup, 2000x2360 hero composite) with zero live HTML headings, over rebuilding the lockup in webfonts + CSS effects
taste.reason: A theatergoer who saw the tube poster must land on a page that is the same object — any webfont approximation of the glitch-RGB 'ONLY HUMAN' would register as a knockoff of the thing it's advertising
evidence: only live display type is footer date band in asap-condensed

taste.name: Depth Comes From Light, Not Gravity
taste.trigger: When components needed separation from a pure-black stage where a conventional dark drop shadow would be invisible
taste.decision: Built elevation from emitted light — zero-offset #B2D1D1 glows (10-33px blur, 1-3 layers) with black inset vignettes — over borders, surface-color steps, or offset shadows; reserved the page's only offset black shadow for the BOOK NOW button
taste.reason: In a theater nothing casts shadows downward; things are lit or unlit. Glowing edges read as spotlights and signage, and the lone object with physical weight is the one you're asked to press — the ticket button
evidence: 5 of 6 shadows are teal zero-offset glows
BOOK NOW carries rgba(0,0,0,.19) 0 10px 20px + second black layer
hover animates text-shadow/box-shadow on the shared 0.3s token — light is the feedback channel

taste.name: One Gel, Three Intensities
taste.trigger: When UI chrome (nav, forms, socials, footer) had to coexist with heavily art-directed teal photography
taste.decision: Locked every CSS color to the photograph's own axis — black stage, #B2D1D1 ice-teal chrome, #05F2DB electric cyan strictly for interactive states — over introducing a neutral gray or a contrasting CTA color (the theater-marketing default red/orange BOOK NOW)
taste.reason: A second hue would sit on top of the scene; keeping chrome on the image's color axis makes buttons feel lit by the same rig as the performer's face, so the interface disappears into the production
evidence: zero pure grays — one incidental #999 in 391 elements
#B2D1D1 triples as text, border, and glow color

taste.name: Chrome Whispers So the Act Can Shout
taste.trigger: When sizing the functional layer — nav, CTA, form labels — against a full-viewport portrait
taste.decision: Pushed UI type DOWN as priority went up: BOOK NOW at 10px/600 is the smallest text on the page, nav 14px tracked caps, labels 9.8-11.2px — over the conventional oversized hero CTA; refused card containers everywhere except the one panel that collects input
taste.reason: Every pixel of loud UI is a pixel of broken illusion. Tracked uppercase micro-type reads as engraved front-of-house signage — findable when you want a ticket, invisible when you're watching the star
evidence: CTA is 10px/600/uppercase — smallest font on page
14px modal size (x29) while 21px+ reserved for editorial ledes
largest CSS grid is a 2-col form row
